General
Vision Marine Technologies Inc. (the “Company,” “Vision Marine,” “we,” “us” or “our”) is a marine technology and recreational boating company engaged in the development and commercialization of electric marine propulsion systems and electric boats, as well as the retail sale and servicing of recreational boats and related marine products.
Prior to June 20, 2025, when we acquired Nautical Ventures Group Inc. (“Nautical Ventures” or “NVG”), our principal activities consisted of the design, development and manufacturing of electric outboard powertrain systems and electric boats, together with the operation of electric boat rental activities. Our core technology is the E-Motion™ high-voltage electric propulsion platform, including our flagship 180-horsepower E-Motion™ 180E outboard system. The platform is designed to provide high-performance electric propulsion through a marine-grade electric motor, integrated control systems, dedicated cooling systems and onboard charging capabilities.
The acquisition of Nautical Ventures significantly expanded our business into the retail sale of new and used recreational boats, marine accessories, parts, maintenance, repair services and marina operations. Nautical Ventures operates a multi-brand recreational boat dealership and marine services business in Florida, offering products powered by both internal combustion engines and electric propulsion systems.
The acquisition materially expanded our revenue base and diversified our operations beyond electric propulsion technology and manufacturing. It also established an additional distribution and service platform through which we may introduce our electric propulsion systems and related products to recreational boating customers.
We currently operate through two reportable segments: Vision Marine, comprising our electric propulsion, electric boat manufacturing and related activities; and Nautical Ventures, comprising our recreational boat dealership, marina, retail and service operations.
For the fiscal year ended August 31, 2026, our consolidated revenue was approximately $58.8 million, of which approximately $57.3 million, or 97.4%, was generated by Nautical Ventures. Substantially all of our consolidated revenue was generated in the United States.
As of August 31, 2026, we had 91 full-time employees.
Organizational History
We were incorporated under the Business Corporations Act (Québec) on August 27, 2012, under the name Riopel Marine, Inc. We changed our name to Vision Marine Technologies Inc. on April 22, 2020.
Our common shares began trading on the Nasdaq Capital Market in November 2020 under the symbol “VMAR.” Our common shares also traded on the TSX Venture Exchange (the “TSXV”) beginning May 1, 2026, until our voluntary delisting, which became effective at the close of trading on August 26, 2026.
As of the date of this Annual Report, we have two directly wholly owned subsidiaries and eleven indirectly wholly owned subsidiaries.
Our principal executive offices are located at 730 Boulevard du Curé-Boivin, Boisbriand, Québec J7G 2A7, Canada, and our telephone number is (450) 951-7009.
Our registered agent in the United States is CorpoMax Inc., located at 2915 Ogletown Road, Newark, Delaware 19713.
Our website address is https://visionmarinetechnologies.com. Information contained on or accessible through our website is not incorporated by reference into this Annual Report. The SEC maintains a website at www.sec.gov that contains reports and other information regarding issuers that file electronically with the SEC.

Transition to U.S. Domestic Issuer Status
As of February 27, 2026, the last business day of our second fiscal quarter, we determined that we no longer qualified as a foreign private issuer under the rules of the SEC. Accordingly, effective September 1, 2026, we became subject to the reporting requirements applicable to U.S. domestic issuers under the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”).
As a U.S. domestic issuer, we are required to file annual reports on Form 10-K, quarterly reports on Form 10-Q and current reports on Form 8-K, and to comply with applicable U.S. proxy rules and other reporting obligations. Our directors, officers and certain shareholders are also subject to the reporting and short-swing profit provisions of Section 16 of the Exchange Act.
In connection with this transition, we elected to prepare our consolidated financial statements for the fiscal year ended August 31, 2026 in accordance with accounting principles generally accepted in the United States (“U.S. GAAP”), rather than International Financial Reporting Standards as issued by the International Accounting Standards Board (“IFRS”).
We are also transitioning from the corporate governance practices applicable to foreign private issuers to those applicable to U.S. domestic issuers, including the applicable Nasdaq corporate governance requirements.
These changes have increased, and are expected to continue to increase, our legal, accounting, administrative and regulatory compliance obligations and related costs.
Recent Developments
Equity Financings.
On December 19, 2025, we completed a best-efforts public offering of common units and pre-funded units, each including one-half of one common warrant, with ThinkEquity LLC acting as placement agent, for aggregate gross proceeds of approximately $9.6 million.
On January 23, 2026, we entered into an at-the-market sales agreement with ThinkEquity LLC providing for the sale of common shares having an aggregate offering price of up to $16,335,000 pursuant to our shelf registration statement on Form F-3 (File No. 333-291917). The at-the-market offering program was completed in July 2026, resulting in aggregate gross proceeds of approximately $16.3 million and net proceeds of approximately $15.5 million.
Reverse Stock Splits.
During fiscal 2026, we effected three reverse stock splits of our outstanding common shares: a 1-for-40 reverse stock split on January 14, 2026, a 1-for-10 reverse stock split on June 17, 2026 and a further 1-for-10 reverse stock split on August 26, 2026.
The August 2026 reverse stock split reduced our then issued and outstanding common shares from approximately 6,530,460 to approximately 653,046, before giving effect to the rounding up of fractional shares, which resulted in the issuance of an additional 63,899 common shares.
Unless otherwise indicated, share and per-share amounts presented in this Annual Report reflect the applicable reverse stock splits.
Annual General Meeting.
At our annual general meeting of shareholders held on February 26, 2026, shareholders elected our directors, ratified the appointment of M&K CPAs, PLLC as our independent registered public accounting firm, adopted an amended and restated restricted share unit plan and an amended and restated stock option plan, and approved certain share-based compensation arrangements for our Chief Executive Officer.

Executive Changes.
On March 1, 2026, we entered into a renewed executive employment agreement with Raffi Sossoyan, our Chief Financial Officer.
On June 19, 2026, we announced the retirement of Roger Moore, founder of Nautical Ventures, from his position as Chief Revenue Officer.
Battery Supplier Developments.
During the third quarter of fiscal 2026, a French-based battery supplier with which we had a commercial dispute entered liquidation proceedings in France. As a result, we recognized an impairment charge of $1,092,925 relating to advances made to that supplier.
We continue to work with alternative battery suppliers to support the development and commercialization of our electric propulsion systems.
Our battery supply relationship with Octillion Power Systems (“Octillion”), a battery manufacturer, remains active. We received two battery packs from Octillion in May 2026, and delivery of an additional 27 battery packs is currently planned for January 2027. The timing of future deliveries remains subject to manufacturing, logistics and other operational considerations.
Normal Course Issuer Bid.

The proposed repurchases were to be conducted pursuant to an issuer repurchase plan agreement with Ventum Financial Corp. No common shares were repurchased under the program.

We have incurred significant operating losses and have not yet achieved sustained profitability. We have made substantial investments in research and development, sales and marketing, and general and administrative activities to develop and expand our business. For the fiscal year ended August 31, 2026, we incurred a net loss of $21,448,990, compared to a net loss of $21,225,873 in fiscal 2025. Our fiscal 2026 net loss included a loss of $8,162,311 attributable to the operations of NVG. As of August 31, 2026, we had an accumulated deficit of $92,425,557.
Although we had cash and cash equivalents of $6,380,935 and positive working capital of $10,269,811 as of August 31, 2026, our history of recurring losses, ongoing financing requirements and uncertainty regarding our ability to achieve sustained profitability raise substantial doubt about our ability to continue as a going concern. Our consolidated financial statements have been prepared on a going concern basis and do not include any adjustments to the carrying amounts or classification of assets and liabilities that might be necessary if we were unable to continue as a going concern.
Our ability to continue operations and execute our business plan depends on generating sufficient cash flows from operations, successfully managing our existing debt obligations, obtaining additional financing when required and achieving sustained profitability. Although the acquisition of NVG has significantly expanded our revenue base, there can be no assurance that its operations or our other business activities will generate sufficient earnings or cash flows to support our ongoing operations and future growth.
We may continue to incur substantial losses, and there can be no assurance that we will achieve or maintain profitability. If our revenues and operating cash flows are insufficient to meet our obligations, we may be required to raise additional capital through debt or equity financings, reduce operating expenditures, delay or cancel planned investments, dispose of assets or otherwise modify our business strategy. Additional financing may not be available on acceptable terms, or at all, and equity financings could result in substantial dilution to existing shareholders.
If we are unable to obtain sufficient financing, generate adequate operating cash flows or achieve profitability, we may be required to significantly curtail or discontinue certain operations, which could materially adversely affect our business, financial condition, results of operations and the value of our common shares.
Limited historical financial information regarding our acquired operations may make it difficult to evaluate our business and future prospects.
On June 20, 2025, we acquired NVG and its subsidiaries, whose operations account for a substantial majority of our consolidated revenues and assets. Although NVG has an established operating history, fiscal 2026 represents the first full fiscal year in which its results have been included in our consolidated financial statements.
Consequently, investors have limited historical consolidated financial information available to evaluate the performance of our combined operations, assess historical trends or predict future operating results. Our historical financial results prior to the acquisition may not be indicative of our future performance, and there can be no assurance that the acquisition will generate the anticipated benefits or improve our financial results.
